summary: Per-tenant SIEM provenance chain + rotating KEK delivery and event traceability playbook
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a tamper-evident per-tenant SIEM export that preserves event traceability across rotated key encryption boundaries and enables deterministic reassembly for forensic playback. They require: monotonic event sequence, per-event provenance token, batch-level KEK-wrapped envelopes, and a clear verification mechanism for auditors.

Impact:
- NorthBridge Financial cannot complete their regulatory evidence submission without provable chain continuity across monthly key rotations.
- Audit window for last quarter at risk of non-compliance if delivered data cannot be cryptographically verified.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted prod in us-west-2.
- Customer is on enterprise tier with Private Connect enabled and S3 archive integration.

Requested delivery and format:
- Hourly batches in newline-delimited canonical JSON-LD (schema v1.3) with: event_seq, tenant_id, event_hash, provenance_token, and parent_batch_ref fields.
- Each batch encrypted with a data key; data keys are wrapped with a KEK that rotates monthly. KEK rotation metadata must be included in the batch manifest.
- An HMAC-SHA256 over the canonicalized batch manifest signed with a per-tenant signing key (KMS-backed) for non-repudiation.

Steps to reproduce / reproduce notes:
- Customer simulated a replay on their side and reported a missing contiguous event_seq range across two batches that span a KEK rotation date.
- They claim verification fails when reconstructing the chain because the provenance_token in the tail of batch N does not link to the head of batch N+1 after rotation.

Observed logs / artifacts provided by customer:
- Example batch manifests (redacted) uploaded to provided S3 bucket (s3://nbf-evidence-uploads/sample-manifests).
- Snippet of verification failure showing: \"provenance_mismatch: expected parent_hash X but got Y\".
- UTC timestamps appear to use local offset in one manifest that caused sort-order differences.

Customer ask / acceptance criteria:
1) Provide a short playbook describing how Redwood guarantees event continuity across KEK rotations and the exact verification steps auditors should perform.
2) Deliver a corrected sample export for the week of 2026-02-01..2026-02-07 that includes canonicalization and rotation metadata.
3) Confirm whether we can include RFC3161-style timestamper signatures for batch manifests as an optional add-on.

Attachments:
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12: Intake - ticket created by Leah after call with NorthBridge compliance. Customer provided sample manifests and a failure trace.
2026-03-12: Reproducer - SRE team replayed canonicalization locally and confirmed inconsistent timezone handling in manifest generator when KEK rotation occurs at midnight UTC in us-west-2.

2026-03-12: Hypothesis - rotation job created new KEK and some in-flight batches were stamped with local time instead of canonical UTC; canonicalization then reordered events when customer applied UTC sort, breaking parent_hash linkage.

2026-03-12: Confirmed - mismatched canonicalization led to different event_hash values for boundary events; KEK wrapping itself was correct (we validated unwrap via KMS audit log), but hash linkage failed due to ordering and timestamp format inconsistency.
2026-03-13: Mitigation - disabled rotation job during reprocessing window and re-emitted canonicalized manifests for test week; hashes now align and provenance verification passes.
2026-03-13: Cross-check - compared KMS key IDs (cmk-0a1b2c) referenced in both batch manifests and KMS audit logs; wrap/unwrap succeeded for both sides of the rotation.

2026-03-13: Follow-up - need a playbook entry and code change to ensure manifest generator uses RFC3339 UTC for timestamp fields and emits event_seq as strictly monotonic per-tenant with no reliance on local timezone.
comments: Leah Park (2026-03-12): Uploaded examples and asked for forensic proof for our next compliance meeting. Requesting target delivery in 3 business days.
Riley Chen (SRE) (2026-03-12): Reproduced locally; timezone canonicalization bug found. Will reprocess sample week after coordinating with infra to pause rotation job.

DevOps (2026-03-13): Paused KEK rotation window from 02:00-03:00 UTC in us-west-2 and queued reprocessing jobs. PR created to normalize timestamps: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8123.
NorthBridge Compliance (2026-03-13): Thank you — can you include instructions auditors should use to validate manifests? We need simple verification steps and expected outputs.
Riley Chen (2026-03-13): Adding playbook draft to ticket and will attach command-line verification snippets (openssl/hmac + JSON-LD canonicalizer).
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13: Short-term resolution - reprocessed the requested week with corrected canonicalization and uploaded to customer S3 under s3://nbf-evidence-uploads/reprocessed/20260201-20260207/.

2026-03-13: Playbook - added verification steps (canonicalize JSON-LD -> compute event_hash -> verify parent_hash chain -> unwrap data key with KMS -> verify HMAC on batch manifest). Confluence draft linked in related_confluence_pages.
2026-03-14: Product follow-up - engineering ticket opened to enforce RFC3339 UTC timestamps in manifest generator and to add an end-to-end test that simulates KEK rotation boundaries (INT-44721).

2026-03-14: Optional add-on - confirmed we can support RFC3161 timestamper signatures for manifests; legal has to sign off on egress of timestamper data. Follow-up task: estimate work and pricing for add-on (Task -> SUP-919010).
Customer acceptance: NorthBridge Compliance acknowledged receipt and verified reprocessed manifests successfully; they requested final signed playbook PDF and a short walkthrough call.
next_steps: Produce final signed playbook PDF and attach to ticket (owner: Riley Chen).
Schedule 45-minute walkthrough with NorthBridge Compliance for 2026-03-16 (owner: Leah Park).
Ship engineering fix to manifest-generator to enforce UTC RFC3339 timestamps and add boundary test (owner: platform-team, PR #8123).
Create pricing estimate for RFC3161 timestamper add-on and route to commercial (owner: ProductOps).
